title: The Alumni
subtitle: Legends never belong to those who live them. No one knows what the ones that follow added to their story.

items.text: The Alumni
Team Timekeeper's Room

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What in the name of Penny Lane is going on out there?
Regulus picks up on the shift in energy like a sour note. She rushes over to the window to look out toward the Foundation's eastern entryway.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What's with all those people heading out? They finally got sick of being locked up in this place, too?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: But what's their angle? Busting out to put on a concert right before the "Storm" hits? Cor, that'd be mad. But you'd have to admire their rockin' spirit.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh, oh! That's Lopera.
Sotheby has, somewhat inexplicably, produced a telescope and joins Regulus as they peer out the window.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: She's leaving too. But what's got everyone in such a hurry?
Not possessed of an abundance of sense for puzzles, the two turn to face the others in the room.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: That's the Pre-Storm Quick Reaction Force she's leaving with. They're probably being dispatched to solve some crisis outside of headquarters.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: A crisis?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh my! Is there anything we can do? Vertin—Huh? Where have Vertin and Sonetto gone off to?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: We might've been able to ask them if we hadn't been thrown in these boring gray rooms again. How dare they take our lovely, comfy Suitcase from us!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: This is just like the first time I got locked up in this pencil-pusher's paradise. I bet those suits are up to something this time, too.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Not to worry though, 'cause this captain has her ways. My dutiful chief mate is already gathering intel.
The room's door creaks open and, right on cue, APPLe floats inside.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain, I ran into Ms. Stranger on the way back. I think she can explain the situation.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ms. Stranger? Wait, you mean that phony captain of the "Free Breeze"?
A sudden chill covers the room as the door widens to reveal the target of Regulus's exclamation. Yet the words don't find purchase on her elegant face.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Team Timekeeper, I wanted to inform you of Ms. Vertin and Sonetto's status.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Ten minutes ago, we received a report on an emergency at the SPDM. They've made their way there via teleport disk.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Hang about, just the two of them? Not fair! Why're we cooped up here when we could be helping out?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Erm, with all due respect, Captain, we do have a job to do.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: The rest of Team Timekeeper will serve as a reserve unit of the Pre-Storm QRF during personnel admission.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Huh! Come to think of it, I did hear someone mentioning us being a reserve. But I thought that just meant we'd be stuck sitting on our hands waiting for something to do.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The First Squad is on their way to the SPDM. They will join the Timekeeper as soon as possible.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Then let's get ready, shall we? Huh, ah, I'll whip up some pain-relieving dew and misty mist spray in a jiffy.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I want the Foundation's fastest car. No, motorbike. Those kids need help, and this rockin' pirate is going to give it to 'em.
The two of them conspire together, poised to begin a heroic rescue mission even if it means running straight into the maw of the coming "Storm."
Druvis, meanwhile, locks eyes with Ms. Stranger.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Might I speak with you in the hallway, Ms. Stranger?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Of course, Ms. Druvis.
The two exit to the corridor, leaving a growing ruckus behind them.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: We won't be leaving headquarters, will we?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: No, but I didn't have the heart to rain on their parade.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Your job is to protect headquarters, now that the First Squad has left.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Dispatch doesn't want the emergency at the SPDM to interrupt the admission process. Both are equally important.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Hasn't the Foundation been recruiting more talent than ever in the past few months? I doubt manpower is a problem anymore.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Is it in any way possible to reassign this duty to another unit so we can reinforce the Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: We have expanded our staff considerably, but many of the new members are from the current era. This is their first "Storm." Their reaction to it could be unpredictable.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Unfortunately, we've determined it's best not to put them on any tasks in the lead-up to it. In fact, we've been keeping them under close surveillance.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It doesn't help that many of them still carry grudges from the war. Not all of them were on the same side.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Still, there's no need to worry for your friends. The First Squad are experienced in dealing with Manus Vindictae. The Timekeeper is in safe hands.
She pauses to listen to the moth beside her ear.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I don't suppose you can manage to pacify them?

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: They're hardly what I would call "obedient."

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Then they'll have to learn to live with it. The Foundation has rules for a reason.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: I'll do my best. But I can't promise anything.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: The first time we came to the Foundation, they also took the Suitcase from Vertin under the guise of "research."

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: I'm afraid there isn't much I can do to dissuade their suspicion, nor their dissatisfaction.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I'm grateful as long as you are willing to try, Ms. Druvis.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: "Razor" will contact you soon to give you further instructions.
Before she leaves, Ms. Stranger pauses at the door to Team Timekeeper's temporary lodgings.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Apparently, neither you nor I like the characters we're playing on this stage.
Broom Closet, Air Raid Shelter

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How's Matilda doing?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Her vitals are strong, and she doesn't appear to have any dangerous wounds, but she still hasn't come to.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Her crystal ball is broken. I suspect it took the brunt of the damage. But we need to get her some professional medical help to know more.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If only Ms. Tooth Fairy weren't at the UK branch with Flutterpage right now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Still, there should be medical staff on-site at the school. Let's move Matilda somewhere safe and start looking.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Vertin!
A dusty, disheveled Merel emerges from the corner.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I've checked the shelter. There aren't any other students or staff. Some walls have collapsed, though. We can't access the other underground facilities.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's no time to clear debris. We'll have to move above ground.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Aren't we going to wait for reinforcements?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No. The clock is ticking. We can't afford to wait.
Sonetto, having already reviewed the manual from cover to cover after receiving their assignment, lowers her head in contemplation.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This tower's Shelter Dove has been destroyed. And the backup can only keep us safe for ten minutes without a pedestal.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And to make matters worse, I don't have my Suitcase. If things go wrong, you could all be infected with the Storm Syndrome.
Merel can't help but look at the Shelter Dove lying on the ground. Though only a few minutes have passed, its glow has dimmed significantly.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So, where should we go now?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Normally, I'd suggest the central watchtower. It's where the instructors used to tell us to go in case of emergencies.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But I don't imagine we'd make it that far with a comatose patient and a child.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Our best choice is the library. It's close by and "Storm"-proof.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: With any luck, we'll find something useful, or at least some other people.
Beneath her calm exterior, new worries surface in the chief assistant's mind.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What if the Manus are already there?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We take them down. And if there are too many of them, we'll pass through it to the clinic. We need to take Matilda there anyway.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The plan is settled then. We'd better get moving. The "Storm" waits for no one.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If combat breaks out, I'll do what I can to protect Matilda and Beverly.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll trust you both to handle whatever stands in our way.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Understood.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: S-Sure. Just leave it to us.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Alright. Grab Beverly, and let's move.
Path, SPDM

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Sonetto!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Regna   sereno   intenso   ed   infinito!
Light flows from the tip of her glasfeder, condenses, then cleaves through the air like a sword.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: *exhalation* Vertin, Beverly, all clear.

items.speaker: Beverly
items.text: Wow!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Stay calm and keep your eyes open. Watch your step.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Vertin? What are you looking at?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nothing. Let's get inside.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The side entrance is right ahead. Keep going.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Let me get the door.
Merel turns. Just as she readies herself to run, the library's side door swings open.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Everyone, get in here. Quickly.
Hallway, Library
The door is slammed shut and a small cadre of students inside slide desks and chairs into place behind them to reinforce it.

items.speaker: Beverly
items.text: Moss! Randy! You're alright!
Beverly runs toward his classmates.
Rows of bookshelves divide the library into a series of compact alcoves, nearly every one of which is now filled with children in white uniforms.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: All these students ...
Lavender stands in shock as she watches the unconscious Matilda being carried into the library.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: What-What happened to Ms. Matilda?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She's wounded. Could you find a quiet room and help me move her there? She may have suffered some trauma to her head, so we need to be very careful.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I remember there were couches in the reading room. Are they still there?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: They are. Do you remember where it is?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Yeah. Vertin, let me help you put Matilda there.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Alright.
Lavender makes a sharp and precise turn to face Sonetto.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Ms. Sonetto, my name is Lavender, Ninth Grade Monitor Assistant. It's an honor to meet you.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: An honor? You know about me?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: You're an SPDM legend! A lot of us know you from the school parade.
Said legend finds herself struggling to accept the sudden burst of praise.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm flattered. It's very nice to meet you, Lavender. Are you the one who led all these students here?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: That's right. I'd just gotten back to the ceremony when the explosions went off. The instructors told us ninth-graders to lead all the students here.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: We're the oldest students and the only ones who have received any real training, so it's our duty to protect the lower grades. But, honestly, thank goodness you showed up.
It's clear she's attempting to seem more in control than she truly feels. The scale and danger of this crisis are far beyond anything she could have prepared for.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Where are the guards and your instructors now?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: I don't know. They just ordered us to head to the library. A few of them came with us, but they're not doing so well.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: They got hurt protecting us from the Manus on our way over.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You know about Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Yes, and the "Storm" too. I was told about it as a part of my role as monitor assistant. All these things that are happening means the "Storm" is about to arrive, doesn't it?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: I-I understand that we're not allowed to talk about it on school grounds, but given the situation ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I think we can make an exception. You need to be prepared for the possible dangers ahead.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Thank you so much, miss. You don't know how relieved I was when I saw you coming to our rescue. So, you were sent here by the Foundation, right?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: That means headquarters already knows what's going on. Will there be more reinforcements?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Yes, and they're already on their way. We'll be safe soon.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Thank goodness! Phew. We'll follow your orders until then. By the way, who's that woman who was carrying Matilda? Is she your assistant?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: That was Vertin, the Foundation's Timekeeper. And, in fact, I'm her chief assistant.
Lavender's eyes open wide in disbelief.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: You mean that was Vertin? THE Vertin?! I heard she ran away from the school and got expelled. How did you come to be her assistant?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, I'm the Vertin you've heard about. But I was never expelled.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: S-Sorry. When did you ...?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's more than alright. It's only natural that people would start rumors with me coming here so rarely.
Lavender never imagined she'd run into so many "campus legends" all at once.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: How could it be? Ah, never mind. I'll do whatever I can to help, Ver—Ms. Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Vertin is just fine, Lavender.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Could you tell me more about the situation here? We need all the details.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Of course, but it might be better to go somewhere that the other students can't hear us.
